query: What are the common advantage attributes of airlines whose overall rating is high?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Service quality is a genuine constitutive aspect of an airline's competitive advantage.

per_column.name: crew_proactive_care
per_column.rationale: A dimension of the service experience; a real aspect of the advantage, though it overlaps heavily with crew_service_quality (both capture crew service excellence).

per_column.name: cultural_service_ethos
per_column.rationale: The style/character of service is an aspect of the service offering, hence part of competitive advantage, but again overlaps the service cluster.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Catering quality is a constitutive part of the product offering that drives advantage.

per_column.name: meal_variety
per_column.rationale: A sub-aspect of the catering offering; a real part but overlaps with food_beverage_quality.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_assessment
per_column.rationale: Seat comfort is a constitutive aspect of the physical product/hard-product advantage.

per_column.name: seat_product_type
per_column.rationale: The hard-product type is an aspect of the seating offering; overlaps with seat_comfort_assessment as a seating cluster.

per_column.name: special_service_recovery
per_column.rationale: Service recovery is a legitimate aspect of the service experience, part of the advantage; overlaps the service cluster.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: Value-for-money is a constitutive commercial facet of competitive advantage, distinct from product/service quality.

judge.rationale: All nine columns are genuine constitutive facets (part-of aspects) of airline competitive advantage rather than external predictors or causes, so the meronymy requirement is met. However mutual exclusivity is weak: the set clusters into three heavily overlapping groups -- service (crew_service_quality, crew_proactive_care, cultural_service_ethos, special_service_recovery), catering (food_beverage_quality, meal_variety), and seating (seat_comfort_assessment, seat_product_type) -- with several columns capturing the same underlying aspect under different names. Exhaustiveness is moderate: soft product (service, food, seat) and value are well covered, but key advantage aspects such as network/route connectivity, schedule/punctuality/reliability, inflight entertainment/connectivity, baggage/loyalty program, and price competitiveness are absent, leaving the concept only partially decomposed.
